title: An ALMA Survey of M-dwarfs in the Beta Pictoris Moving Group with two new debris disc detections
question: Are M-dwarf debris discs intrinsically less common than around earlier types, or just hard to detect at the wavelengths and sensitivities of earlier far-IR surveys? Tested with an ALMA Band 7 survey of BPMG M-dwarfs.

recipe.method: Provided ALMA pipeline script in CASA, then time and channel averaging for continuum imaging
key_parameters: 30 s averaging and two channels per spectral window

recipe.goal: Make continuum images and inspect for extended emission
recipe.method: Naturally weighted CLEAN images; additional 1 and 2 arcsec uv tapers inspected visually

recipe.goal: Measure point-source flux at each Gaia DR3 stellar position
recipe.method: Point-source model fit to visibilities with CASA uvmodelfit at the Gaia DR3 location; offsets fixed except for detections and near-detections
key_parameters: Stars separated by less than the beam are listed as one with the mean of two uvmodelfit fluxes

recipe.goal: Estimate stellar photosphere flux and derive mm excess
recipe.method: SED fitting of model atmospheres to photometry (Yelverton19 method) to predict 880 um stellar flux; subtract from measured flux to get excess; 3 sigma criterion for detection
Split observations into individual scans, re-image and check flux variance over time
Continuum-subtracted CLEAN images made with uvcontsub, searched at the stellar location and near the expected stellar radial velocity

recipe.goal: Stack non-detections for a mean upper limit
recipe.method: Stack images of 21 non-detections with the star within 0.5 arcsec of the phase centre; read flux at centre and RMS
Search primary-beam-corrected CLEAN images within 10 arcsec of phase centre for sources of at least 5 sigma; compare to galaxy number counts

recipe.goal: Constrain disc fractional luminosity and temperature for detections
recipe.method: Fit SED/dust models to get fractional luminosity-temperature distribution, then restrict by disc radius (resolved radius or beam-size upper limit) converted to a mm grain temperature
key_parameters: GJ 2006 A radius limit 34 au gives T lower limit 25 K; AT Mic A radius limit 10 au gives T lower limit 40 K; GSC 07396-00759 radius 70.2 au gives T of 20 K
assumptions: Unresolved discs: beam semi-major axis sets an upper limit on disc radius

recipe.goal: Compute detection rate and completeness-adjusted rate
recipe.method: Count detections in the 36-star sample; for each detection compute completeness (fraction of observations that would have detected that disc flux), divide and sum; binomial small-number uncertainties; test with one million synthetic detection sets
key_parameters: Synthetic discs: radius uniform 10-100 au, fractional luminosity log-uniform 1e-7 to 1e-3, host luminosity drawn from sample without replacement
assumptions: Large assumptions about the underlying M-dwarf disc population in the synthetic test
